hints: Apply integration by parts with $u = \ln(3x)$ and $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x} = x^2$.
Evaluate the antiderivative between $x = 1$ and $x = 3$, writing the answer in the form $a\ln b + c$ with exact rational coefficients.
walkthrough:
Set up integration by parts with $u = \ln(3x)$ and $v' = x^2$:
$$u' = \dfrac{1}{3x} \cdot 3 = \dfrac{1}{x}$$
$$v = \dfrac{x^3}{3}$$

Apply the integration by parts formula $\int u v'\,\mathrm{d}x = uv - \int u'v\,\mathrm{d}x$:
$$\int x^2\ln(3x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{x^3}{3}\ln(3x) - \int \left(\dfrac{x^3}{3}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{x^3}{3}\ln(3x) - \dfrac{1}{3}\int x^2\,\mathrm{d}x$$

Subtract the lower limit from the upper limit:
$$\text{Integral} = (18\ln 3 - 3) - \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\ln 3 - \dfrac{1}{9}\right)$$
$$= \left(18 - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\ln 3 - \left(3 - \dfrac{1}{9}\right)$$
$$= \left(\dfrac{54}{3} - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\ln 3 - \left(\dfrac{27}{9} - \dfrac{1}{9}\right)$$
$$= \dfrac{53}{3}\ln 3 - \dfrac{26}{9}$$

State the exact result in the required form $a\ln b + c$:
$$\dfrac{53}{3}\ln 3 - \dfrac{26}{9}$$
with rational $a = \dfrac{53}{3}, c = -\dfrac{26}{9}$ and integer $b = 3$.

ai_rubric.Integration by Parts: Applies integration by parts to obtain $\frac{x^3}{3}\ln(3x) - \frac{1}{3}\int x^2 dx$ (M1A1). Completes integration to $\frac{x^3}{3}\ln(3x) - \frac{x^3}{9}$ (A1). Substitutes limits 1 and 3 correctly (DM1). Obtains exact result $\frac{53}{3}\ln 3 - \frac{26}{9}$ (A1).
